title: SettingsState
description: Response of `GET /settings` and of a `PATCH /settings` that was written.

file_error.description:
Why allotd rejects `config.toml`, if it does. Settings cannot be changed until the
file is fixed by hand.

listening_port.description: The port allotd listens on, which differs from `daemon.port` until a restart.

pending_restart.description: Keys whose saved value takes effect only once allotd restarts, such as `daemon.port`.

revision.description: The revision of `config.toml`, to send with the next `PATCH /settings`.

spec.description: Every setting allotd owns, with its page, control, range, default, label and help.

values.description:
The value of every setting on the spec's pages: the file's, or while allotd rejects the
file, the last good values, which stay in effect.

Bound.description: One end of a number's range.

exclusive.description: Whether the limit itself is out of range.

label.description: The value as the panel shows it.

value.description: The value written to the file.

HeavyRule.description:
Marks a simple command as heavy when its program and arguments match.

Matching ignores case, and `*` matches any run of characters.

args.description:
Any one of these makes the command heavy; empty matches any arguments. A pattern that
starts with `-` matches that flag anywhere in the command; any other pattern matches
the first positional argument (the first one not starting with `-` or `+`).

class.description: Class the matched command needs a lease for.

program.description: Program name without directory or extension, for example `cargo` or `python*`.

JobClass.description: Named job profiles. Their values come from the `[classes]` section of the config.

oneOf.description: Short jobs that barely load the machine.
Compiles, test suites, and other CPU-bound work.
Training, rendering, games, and other GPU-bound work.
Jobs that load both the CPU and the GPU.

JobProfile.description: Resources a job is expected to need while it runs.

cores.description: Logical cores the job keeps busy.

gpu_pct.description: GPU engine load as a percentage of one adapter.

OffSwitch.description: A switch that turns a numeric feature off by writing one value.

label.description: The switch's label, describing the on state.

value.description: The value written while the switch is off.

Platform.description: An operating system a panel runs on.

oneOf.description: The Windows tray.
The macOS menu bar app.
The GNOME extension and the KDE widget.
A share from 0 to 100.
A number of job runs.
A number of days.
A duration in seconds; panels may show it in minutes or hours.
Logical cores; fractions are allowed.
Memory in megabytes; panels may show it in gigabytes.
A TCP port, shown without digit grouping.

Requirement.description: A switch another setting depends on.

note.description: Shown under the disabled setting while the switch is off.

Revision.description: A version of `config.toml`'s bytes, as 16 hex digits.

RowName.description: The name field of a row the user adds or renames.

pattern.description:
A regular expression the whole name must match. A name must also differ from every
other row's and from every class's.

oneOf.description: On or off.

default.description: The value while the key is not in the file.

oneOf.description: A number in a unit, written to the file in that unit.

automatic.description:
How the value is worked out while the key is left out, when it may be, shown
beside an Automatic choice.

default.description:
The value while the key is not in the file. In a table's fields, the value a new
row starts with, or `None` when a new row must give one or `automatic` applies.

integer.description: Whether only whole numbers are allowed.

max.description: The largest value allowed, if any besides `max_key`.

max_key.description: A setting this value must be at most, by key; in a table, a field of the same row.

min.description: The smallest value allowed, if any besides `min_key`.

min_key.description: A setting this value must be at least, by key; in a table, a field of the same row.

off.description: A switch in front of the number, when one value turns the feature off.

quantity.description: What the number counts, which picks its unit and display.

oneOf.description: A line of text, never blank.

pattern.description: A regular expression the whole text must match, if any.

oneOf.description: One of a fixed set of values.

default.description: The value a new item starts with, or `None` when one must be picked.

oneOf.description: A list of strings without blank entries; a list in the file replaces the default list.

default.description: The list while the key is not in the file.

oneOf.description:
Named rows of sizes, such as `[classes.cpu_heavy]`, edited one row at a time. A row
in the file changes only the fields it names.

new_row_name.description:
How a row added by the user is named, or `None` when rows cannot be added,
renamed or deleted.

rows.description: The built-in rows with their defaults, which always exist.

oneOf.description:
An ordered list of heavy-command rules, always written whole. A list in the file, even
an empty one, replaces the default list; removing the key brings the default back.

default.description: The list while the key is not in the file.

SettingSpec.description: One setting: a key of `config.toml`, or a field of a table row or rule.

advanced.description: Whether the setting is rarely changed and shows last on its page, under Advanced.

control.description: How the value is edited, with its default and range.

help.description: One or two plain sentences. Panels show the key after them.

key.description:
The TOML key: a dotted path such as `admission.headroom_pct` for a setting on a page,
or the key inside a row, such as `cores`, for a field of a table or rule.

label.description: A noun phrase in sentence case; a switch's label describes the on state.

needs_restart.description: Whether a change takes effect only once allotd restarts.

platforms.description: The operating systems whose panels show the setting; empty means every one.

requires.description: A switch that must be on for this setting to act; panels disable it while it is off.

SettingValue.description:
The value of one setting on a page, keyed like the spec, in the kind its control edits.

The tags end in `_value`, so the panels' generated types never share a name with
[`SettingControl`]'s: System.Text.Json's source generator warns on a repeated type name.

oneOf.description: The state of a switch.
A number, in the unit of its setting.
A list of strings, such as `classifier.light_flags`.
The heavy-command rules.
Every row of a size table, built-in rows included.

value.description: The rows: classes in class order, presets by name.

SettingsGroupSpec.description: A titled group of settings on a page.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique on its page, such as `learn`.

SettingsPageSpec.description: A page of the Settings window.

intro.description: A sentence under the title, if the page has one.

SettingsSpec.description:
Every allotd setting, page by page, in the order the Settings window shows them.

Panels add what holds no key themselves: the Panel page of their own settings, live
explanations, the command test, the service status, the config file row and Reset.

SizeRow.description: A class or preset with its values.

min_cores.description: The fewest cores a lease of it may start with; `None` while it is automatic.

name.description: The row's key in the file, such as `cpu_heavy` or a preset's name.

profile.description: What a lease of it asks for.

SizeRowSpec.description: A built-in row of a size table.

default.description: The row's values while the file does not change them.

default_min_cores.description:
The row's minimum cores while the file names none; `None` follows the field's
automatic rule.

label.description: The row as the panel shows it.

name.description: The row's key in the file, such as `cpu_heavy`.
